Student debt passed $1.2 Trillion last year. and here's a cost comparison But hey, at least the defense industry lobbyists recycle some of the $Trillion a year as Citizen United campaign donations to keep the gravy flowing.

While I don't support the military entirely, I do believe the F-35 project was reasonable considering the time and budget. What we often forget is these planes will have to last generations before getting 'updated' or replaced, we have to plan for the future. Additionally, the F-35 probably won't even be the most common jet in the military, what will happen is parts in the f-35 will be installed in other jets. So in some jets we'll have the F-35's stealth engine, in others just the main canon, in some the vertical take off, but the F-35 will have all the bells and whistles.

Lastly, we'll likely make our money back from this project, most every other military in the world buys or leases weapons from the U.S. Sure the project wasn't cheap, but neither will the product, and we have a rather large market to sell to
